question: Should OpenClaw use one unified sub-agent intervention policy for absolute-deadline warnings and inactivity nudges, and what delivery guarantee should native and ACP children receive?
rationale: The capability remains missing, but its durable API depends on whether warning delivery is guaranteed, best-effort, or unsupported per runtime and whether it shares configuration with the open inactivity-recovery proposal.

options.title: Unified lifecycle policy
options.body: Implement one intervention subsystem with separate deadline and inactivity triggers, shared delivery semantics, and coordinated timer ownership.

options.title: Deadline warning only
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped pre-timeout warning and explicitly document any weaker ACP behavior where equivalent steering is unavailable.

options.title: Keep hard deadlines
options.body: Retain hard timeouts and post-timeout recovery without adding another runtime control or configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Unified lifecycle policy
recommendation.body: Implement one intervention subsystem with separate deadline and inactivity triggers, shared delivery semantics, and coordinated timer ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the existing timeout configuration and the native, ACP, and announcement lifecycle surfaces involved in this decision.
